python -c "
import humanize
import datetime as dt

for days in [29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35]:
    # Test with my simple fix: zero out days if <= 0.5 and months > 0
    suppress_set = {humanize.time.Unit.MICROSECONDS, humanize.time.Unit.MILLISECONDS}
    min_unit = humanize.time.Unit.SECONDS
    
    delta_days = days
    delta = dt.timedelta(days=delta_days)
    
    date, delta_obj = humanize.time._date_and_delta(delta, precise=True)
    suppress_set = humanize.time._suppress_lower_units(min_unit, set())
    
    years, days_rem = humanize.time._quotient_and_remainder(
        delta.days, 365, humanize.time.Unit.YEARS, min_unit, suppress_set, '%0.2f')
    months, days = humanize.time._quotient_and_remainder(
        days_rem, 30.5, humanize.time.Unit.MONTHS, min_unit, suppress_set, '%0.2f')
    
    # Apply fix
    if months > 0 and days <= 0.5:
        days = 0.0
    
    # Continue conversion to get hours etc.
    secs = days * 24 * 3600 + delta.seconds
    days, secs = humanize.time._quotient_and_remainder(
        secs, 24*3600, humanize.time.Unit.DAYS, min_unit, suppress_set, '%0.2f')
    
    hours, secs = humanize.time._quotient_and_remainder(
        secs, 3600, humanize.time.Unit.HOURS, min_unit, suppress_set, '%0.2f')
    
    minutes, secs = humanize.time._quotient_and_remainder(
        secs, 60, humanize.time.Unit.MINUTES, min_unit, suppress_set, '%0.2f')
    
    print(f'{days}d -> m={months}, d={days}, h={hours}, m={minutes}')
